corrections: MARIA NICOTRA'S FATHER, and the man the Queensland death registration of 1963 calls «John Nicotra» and nothing else. Here he is in his own act: «sono comparsi GIOVANNI NICOTRA, di anni trentuno, di professione bracciante, DOMICILIATO E RESIDENTE A MASCALI, figlio di ROSARIO, di professione bracciante, e di VENERA MURABITO, contadina, domiciliati e residenti PURE IN MASCALI». A father six years younger in three years — TWO DECLARED AGES THAT DO NOT AGREE. «Di anni TRENTUNO» at his marriage on 7 October 1872, which puts his birth about 1841; «di anni VENTOTTO» at his daughter Maria's birth on 10 December 1875, which puts it about 1847. Six years the wrong way in three. KEPT AS A CONFLICT rather than averaged: his own birth act at Mascali, in either 1841 or 1847, would settle it and would carry his parents Rosario Nicotra and Venera Murabito independently. The identification of the two men does NOT rest on the age -- it rests on the wife, VENERA CASSANITI, named in both acts, and on the comune.

Age — two acts disagree by five years — THE TWO ACTS THAT NAME HIM GIVE AGES THAT CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT. Piedimonte Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 makes him THIRTY-ONE in October 1872, so born about 1841. Mascali Nati 1873 atto 145 makes him TWENTY-SIX in December 1873, so born about 1847. He should be thirty-two by the second act and is declared six years younger. It is the same man — the wife is VENERA CASSANITI FU GAETANO in both, aged twenty-four in each, and the father is ROSARIO in both — so this is a declared age and not a different household. This archive's own audit says declared ages run one to four years out as a matter of routine; six is past that, and NEITHER YEAR IS ADOPTED. His birth is between about 1841 and about 1847 and the register that would settle it is Giarre, where he says he was born.

Surname — the spelling is an informant's, not a record's — PROBABLY VENERA CASSANITI. «Cassaneti» appears exactly once in the whole Queensland index -- on her daughter's 1963 death registration, taken down from an informant at a Brisbane registry -- and NOWHERE ELSE. «CASSANITI» returns five Queensland registrations and is the ordinary Catanese form; it is also what the PIEDIMONTE ETNEO birth index writes, holding a Cassaniti Sebastiano and a Cassaniti Leonardo Maria in 1875 alone. THIS MATTERS PRACTICALLY: a Sicilian register searched for «Cassaneti» will return nothing and the negative will mean nothing. Search Cassaniti.

A surname the Queensland registrar invented — VENERA CASSANITI, born about 1848 at Piedimonte Etneo, daughter of the late GAETANO CASSANITI and the late MARIA CURRENTI. «CASSANETI» appears nowhere in Italy and exactly once in the whole Queensland index -- on Maria Mazza's own death registration, taken down from an informant at a Brisbane registry counter. corrections: The tree gives him no source at all, and gives him two children, Rocco and Guiseppe. THE REGISTER GIVES HIM NEITHER. Across 1856, 1858, 1859 and 1860 he and Giovanna Zirilli have Domenico (1856), Domenico (1859) and Maria Annunziata (1860); the Rocco and Giuseppe the tree assigns him belong to Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta. His first son being Domenico twice suggests, on naming custom alone, that his own father was a Domenico Arena -- a lead, not a finding.

Generation — a lead, RETRACTED — THIS ARCHIVE WITHDRAWS ITS OWN INFERENCE. From Orazio naming two sons Domenico, naming custom suggested his father was a Domenico Arena. Two Orazio Arena births at Scilla now say otherwise: act 10 of 1821 gives him a father GIUSEPPE (and the tree's own year, 1821, exactly), and act 1 of 1833 gives a different Orazio a father BONAVENTURA. Neither is a Domenico. The mistake was not the custom but the assumption behind it: the first child this archive had FOUND was not necessarily his FIRST child. The years 1850-1855 are unread, and a son Giuseppe in one of them would restore the custom exactly. Recorded as a candidate: ORAZIO ARENA b. 14 DECEMBER 1821, son of Giuseppe Arena and a Teresa. FURTHER EVIDENCE, BOTH WAYS: Orazio's earliest known child is a DAUGHTER, Teresa, born 17 October 1853. Custom names the first daughter for her paternal grandmother, and act 10 of 1821 makes Orazio's mother a Teresa -- which SUPPORTS the 1821 candidate. But that same act makes his father a Giuseppe, and Orazio's first son is Domenico, with 1852-1855 now read and no earlier son. The two halves disagree and the archive is not picking one.

corrections: The first child of the 1872 marriage — BORN AT MASCALI ON 12 DECEMBER 1873, fourteen months after her parents' marriage, and named for her mother -- or for her father's mother Venera Murabito; both are Venera, so the custom points two ways and settles nothing on its own. THE ACT ITSELF IS NOT YET OPENED, so the mother is inferred from the household and not read. Index entry only.

Birth date, birth hour and birthplace — BORN AT MASCALI ON 12 DECEMBER 1873 AT ONE IN THE AFTERNOON, in contrada NOCILLE, and registered the next day by her father in person. «è comparso GIOVANNI NICOTRA di ROSARIO d'anni ventisei di professione lavorante ... una Bambina di sesso feminile ... nata il giorno dodici del corrente mese alle ore tredici dalla di lui moglie VENERA CASSANITI fu GAETANO d'anni ventiquattro ... alla quale figlia dichiara di dare il nome di VENERA». She is the FIRST CHILD of the marriage of 7 October 1872, born fourteen months after it, and she is named VENERA — which on Sicilian custom is the paternal grandmother's name, and the paternal grandmother is VENERA MURABITO.

The naming custom, tested twice and fitting twice — THE ORDER OF THE DAUGHTERS IS WHAT SICILIAN CUSTOM PREDICTS, AND IT NAMES BOTH GRANDMOTHERS. First daughter for the paternal grandmother, second for the maternal. Giovanni Nicotra and Venera Cassaniti married on 7 October 1872 and their first two daughters are VENERA, born 12 December 1873, and MARIA, born 8 December 1875. The paternal grandmother is VENERA MURABITO and the maternal grandmother is MARIA CURRENTI. Both fit, in the right order, and neither name was chosen by this archive. The same argument already runs for the sons: the export gives the couple a Rosario and the marriage act names the groom's father ROSARIO. THREE FOR THREE IS CUSTOM AND NOT PROOF — a Venera and a Maria are two of the commonest names in these registers — but it is independent of the acts and it points the same way.

name: Domenica Costa
registerSources: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
registerNote: Filippo Arena's wife, and now one of the best-attested people in this archive: her baptism of 1787, her marriage of 1815, her son's birth in 1819. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are GIOVANNI DE COSTA, dead at Scilla on 29 March 1790 when she was two, and MARTA ALFONZETTI, who was still alive to consent to the marriage twenty-five years later. NOTE THE SURNAME: Costa is also what her great-grandson Rocco married, in Generosa Costa, and a Lorenzo Costa was lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. THIS ROW ONCE SAID «HER MARRIAGE IS OUT OF REACH». It was in a volume nobody had opened, four years before the window this archive had drawn for itself.

name: Domenica Romano
registerNote: Candeloro Donato's wife. Not in the family tree.

name: Domenico Arena
registerNote: AN ARENA HOUSEHOLD AT SCILLA WITH NO ESTABLISHED CONNECTION TO THIS FAMILY, and it is recorded here as exactly that. He is a BARBER where the spine is four generations of sailors, and the only Arena this archive has who was alive in the 1740s. His wife is ANNA MELIDONI and his eldest son DIEGO ARENA, sartore, married Maria Giuseppa Pontillo in 1813. HE IS NOT CLAIMED AS ORAZIO ARENA'S FATHER, and the temptation to claim him is the reason this note exists: Scilla has more than one Arena family, and TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE sharing a surname in one small town is how this archive nearly hung a birth act on the wrong Mariano Mazza a week ago. What would settle it is Orazio Arena's own marriage, which is pre-1809 and parish.

name: Domenico Arena
registerNote: FILIPPO ARENA'S THIRD BROTHER. The 1838 Tavola opens on him: «ARENA DOMENICO e POLISTINA TERESA -- FU ORAZIO, e Lett.a Morabito». He married TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 4 September 1838. HE IS ALSO THE MAN WHO DATES HIS FATHER'S DEATH: the «fu» before Orazio is the only one in any Arena entry this archive has read, and it brackets Orazio's death to the ten years after August 1828. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Domenico Arena, barbiere, born about 1743 who appears in the 1813 marriage of Diego Arena -- that one is two generations up and no connection is claimed.

name: Domenico Arlotta
registerNote: THE DEEPEST PERSON THIS ARCHIVE HAS REACHED ON THE CALABRIAN SIDE. Named only as 'il fu Domenico' in his son Giovanni Arlotta's own words, in the birth act of his great-grandson Giovanni Arena, 30 April 1854. A great-great-great-great-great-grandfather of Mia and Rocco. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. TIGHTENED BY TWENTY-SIX YEARS: he is «FU Domenico Arlotta» in his son's marriage act of 30 AUGUST 1828, so dead before then, not merely before April 1854. AND HE HAS A WIFE NOW: ANNA BARBARO, who was alive at that wedding.

name: Domenico Arlotta
registerSources: Scilla, Morti 1915, parte I, atto 34 — read in the original
registerNote: SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S BROTHER, and the act names both their parents: «da fu GIOVANNI e da fu COSTA MARIA». A MARINARO, husband of MARIA PONTILLO, dead at noon on 14 March 1915 at the RIONE CHIANALEA. He carries his grandfather's name -- the DOMENICO ARLOTTA this archive knows only from «figlio del fu Domenico» in an 1854 birth act -- which is what the naming custom predicts and is not proof of him.

name: Domenico Ventrice
registerSources: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
registerNote: Giovanna Ventrice's paternal grandfather, and the reason his certificate is in her marriage bundle: the act says she produced «la fede di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno», and the bundle holds exactly two Ventrice deaths. Died at Zambrone on 13 January 1815 at twenty-three o'clock, a BRACCIALE, husband of ANNA FAMA, and son of the late PAOLO VENTRICE and the late ANNA PAPPA. HIS AGE IS AMBIGUOUS IN THE ONLY SURVIVING TEXT: the copyist writes «sposo di Anna Fama di anni cinquanta ... di anni cinquantotto, di professione bracciale». The fifty-eight sits with his trade and is taken as his, so born about 1757; the fifty is taken as his wife's. This archive first published him as fifty.

name: Filippo Arena
registerSources: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
registerNote: Named in FOUR independent acts. The sea trade runs Orazio -> Filippo -> Francesco Antonio -> Rocco, four generations of sailors, and he was a MARINARO himself at twenty-two. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. HE WAS ALSO, FOR FIVE DAYS, THE ARCHIVE'S PUBLISHED WALL -- «his marriage to Domenica Costa is pre-civil, the Arena line stops here» -- because this archive believed Scilla's registers began in 1816. THEY BEGIN IN 1809. He married Domenica Costa on 12 NOVEMBER 1815, Matrimoni atto 29, and the act names his parents ORAZIO ARENA and LITTERIA MORABITO, both alive and both standing beside him, because at twenty-two he was still a minor under the code. Every negative reported for 1816 to 1819 was correct; the conclusion drawn from them was not. AND HE COULD WRITE: he signed his own marriage act «Filippo Arena sposo», and signed his son's birth act in 1819, in registers where almost nobody signs.

name: Filippo Arena
registerNote: GENERATION NINE. «FIGLIO DEL FU FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO» -- the death act of his son ORAZIO, 12 July 1830. The «fu» dates him dead before that day; his son was born about 1751, so he belongs to the 1720s and everything about him is pre-civil and parish. AND HE EXPLAINS A NAME: Orazio's first son, born 25 March 1793, is FILIPPO -- the Sicilian and Calabrian custom giving the first son his father's father. This archive used the custom to RANK candidates for four months and never once to identify one; here the act confirms it after the fact, which is the only way round that is safe. THERE ARE NOW THREE FILIPPO ARENA in this archive: this one, his grandson born 1793, and that man's grandson born 1852. All three are filed apart on purpose.

name: Filippo Arena
registerNote: Rocco Arena's eldest brother, named for their grandfather Filippo. Not in the family tree.

name: Fortunata Polistina
registerNote: A THIRD CHILD OF GIUSEPPE POLISTENA AND ANNA PONTILLO, and so a third sibling of Camillo Antonio -- after Rocco (13 December 1833) and Annunziata (2 December 1836). The three of them fall three years apart, twice, which is what fixes Rocco as the eldest and pushes Camillo Antonio's birth to 1841 or later. Her act has not been opened. Not in the family tree.

name: Fortunato Arena
registerNote: A son of ROCCO ARENA'S BROTHER Giovanni, dead at ten days. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His death act fixes the household at VIA GROTTE -- the same street where his brother Giuseppe would be born thirteen months later, at number 75 -- and calls his father a PESCATORE, as Giuseppe's birth act does.

name: Francesco Antonio Arena
registerNote: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE, which puts Rocco Arena under Orazio Arena instead. He and Serafina Arlotta have a son Giuseppe on 5 March 1860 and a son Rocco on 20 December 1861 -- exactly the sibling pair the tree assigns to Orazio.

records.what: Scilla, Nati 1854, atto 76 — named as the father, aged 34, marinaro

corrections: The act calls him ANTONIO ARENA, dropping the Francesco, as the 1853 and 1861 acts also do. Born 25 November 1819, he is EXACTLY thirty-four in April 1854 — which is what identifies him.

name: Francesco Cichello
registerNote: CATERINA CICHELLO'S FATHER, named in his daughter's marriage act of 2 March 1824 as «il fu Francesco» -- already dead. Entirely new to this archive, and one of the two people row 34 of the work list existed to find. Not in the family tree.

name: Francesco Crupi
registerNote: ANGELA CRUPI'S FATHER. Named only because his children's Queensland death registrations name him -- and as of today there are FOUR of them, not one. Angela (d. 1973), PIETRO (d. 1961), ANTONINO (d. 1982) and MARIO (d. 1989) all register the same two parents, FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO. A whole Sicilian sibling group in Brisbane, of which this archive knew one. Not in the family tree.

name: Francesco Giovanni Rocco Arena
registerNote: A NEPHEW OF ROCCO ARENA -- son of his brother Giuseppe and Maria Martello -- dead at ten months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His three given names are his paternal grandfather and both his uncles: FRANCESCO for Francesco Antonio Arena, GIOVANNI and ROCCO for his father's brothers.

name: Gaetano Bonanno
registerSources: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
registerNote: Leonarda Bonanno's father. The archive had only the bare first name 'Gaetano', from a marriage proclamation of 1910; he is now in two registers with his surname, his trade and his age. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «figlia del VIVENTE GAETANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi», in his daughter Leonarda's publication certificate. Aged about sixty-four and still at Piedimonte.

name: Gaetano Cassaniti
registerSources: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original
registerNote: VENERA CASSANITI'S FATHER, of Piedimonte Etneo, and DEAD BY OCTOBER 1872: his daughter's marriage act calls her «figlia del FU GAETANO». He is also the father named in her birth entry in the annual Tavola of Nati 1848, act 45, which is what ties the birth to the marriage. MIND THE NAMESAKE: Piedimonte held a GAETANO BONANNO and a GAETANO BONACCORSO at the same period, both braccianti, and this is a third Gaetano again.

name: Gaetano Mazza
registerNote: ANOTHER SON OF ROSARIO AND LEONARDA, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM TOO. «Mazza Rosario, di anni trentadue, bracciante» declared him, born to «BONANNO LEONARDA, industriosa, sua moglie» in VIA S. BASILIO -- the same lane as his brother Mariano eight years earlier, and the mother's surname is given in full, which is what tells this household apart from the other Rosario-and-Leonarda in the town. GAETANO is the name the Sicilian custom gives after the MOTHER'S FATHER, and Leonarda's father is GAETANO BONANNO, named as such in the 1872 and 1873 acts. Witnesses Dimauro Salvatore, twenty-two, and Zappala Sebastiano, twenty-four. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought.

name: Generosa Polistena
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 1 June 1915 (Antonio Costa)
registerNote: GENEROSA COSTA'S PATERNAL GRANDMOTHER — AND THE REASON FOR HER NAME. Southern Italian custom gives the first daughter her paternal grandmother's name, and Generosa Costa, who married Rocco Arena in December 1888, carries this woman's exactly. IT ALSO PUTS A POLISTENA INSIDE THE COSTA LINE a generation before the Polistena quarter's own marriages, which is worth noticing in a town where four of this family's quarters keep intermarrying.

name: Gennaro Melluso
registerNote: GREGORIO MELLUSO'S FATHER. NOT A NEW FINDING -- his son's Queensland death registration of 1971 has been in `data/qld-bdm.tsv` for days. What is new is that he is now a PERSON here rather than a cell in a spreadsheet, which is the only way he reaches the reader. Not in the family tree.

name: Giacoma Turco
registerSources: Scilla, processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di morte di Giovanni Costa
registerNote: GENERATION NINE. «Filius quondam Josephi et Jacobae Turco» -- the QUONDAM governs both parents, so she too was dead by March 1790. NOTE THE SURNAME: the priest who heard her son's last confession on his deathbed was REV. D. PAOLO TURCO. In a town of this size that is very likely a relative at the bedside, not a coincidence, though nothing here proves it. Not in the family tree.

name: Giovanni Arlotta
registerNote: Serafina Arlotta's father, so Rocco Arena's maternal grandfather. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. A sailor. NOW IN THREE ACTS AND DATED: the marriage act of 1851, his daughter's birth act of 1830, and the birth act of 1854 in which he appears IN PERSON, aged seventy-five, to declare his grandson -- and which names HIS OWN FATHER, Domenico.

name: Giovanni Costa
registerNote: DOMENICA COSTA'S FATHER, AND THE OLDEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE. His daughter's marriage bundle carries the parish death register verbatim: «Die vigesima nona mensis Martii Anno Domini millesimo septingentesimo nonagesimo, Scyllae, JOANNES DE COSTA, aetatis suae annorum quadraginta circiter, FILIUS QUONDAM JOSEPHI ET JACOBAE TURCO, legitimus vir MARTHAE ALFONZETTI» -- lying ill in bed, confessed to Rev. D. Paolo Turco, given the Viaticum and anointed, and buried in the church of S. Maria di Porto Salvo. He is written DE COSTA in Latin and COSTA in the civil act. Not in the family tree.

name: Giuseppe Antonio Arlotta
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 2 June 1918
registerNote: A THIRD CHILD OF GIOVANNI ARLOTTA AND MARIA COSTA, husband of ANGELA NUNZIATA PIZZARELLO. Serafina Arlotta was an only child in this archive until today; she now has three documented siblings.

name: Giuseppe Arena
registerNote: FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER, AND THE FIRST SIBLING THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER FOUND FOR HIM. Same parents, same trade, same town: «figlio di ORAZIO ARENA, di professione MARINARO, e di LITTERIA MORABITO». He married MARIA TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 13 November 1821, the promessa taken six days earlier before Tommaso Cutelli, the same sindaco who married Filippo in 1815. THE AGES ARE TIGHT: Filippo was born 25 March 1793 and Giuseppe's age puts him in 1794, eight to twenty months later -- possible, and equally possible that one declared age is a year out, which is routine here. NOTE THE NAME: the family tree holds a GIUSEPPE ARENA born 1860, son of Francesco Antonio -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE two generations apart, and the later one is named for this one, which is what the naming custom predicts.

name: Giuseppe Arena
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Giuseppe Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/03/1925, Padre Domenico, Madre Teresa Polistena, Coniuge Serafina Vita»
registerNote: A CHILD OF FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER DOMENICO, and the first evidence that the 1838 marriage produced anyone. He died at Scilla on 27 March 1925, husband of SERAFINA VITA. THE ENTRY ALSO CONFIRMS TERESA POLISTINA INDEPENDENTLY: this archive had her only from the 1838 annual Tavola, and here she is again as a mother, eighty-seven years later, in a different series indexed by a different hand. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Giuseppe Arena born about 1794 who is Filippo's brother, and from the Giuseppe Arena born 1860 who is Rocco's -- three men of the name in three generations of one extended family, which is what the naming custom does to an archive.

name: Giuseppe Costa
registerSources: Scilla, processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di morte di Giovanni Costa
registerNote: GENERATION NINE, and reached by three documents stacked on each other: the 1815 civil marriage act named Domenica Costa's father; the marriage bundle copied his parish death act; and that act calls him «FILIUS QUONDAM JOSEPHI ET JACOBAE TURCO». QUONDAM is the whole finding -- Giuseppe was already dead when his son died in March 1790. Nothing else is known of him and nothing else is likely to be: Scilla's civil registers begin nineteen years after his son's death. Not in the family tree.

name: Giuseppe Polistena
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 19 October 1924 (Camillo Antonio Polistena)
registerNote: A NEW ANCESTOR ON THE THINNEST QUARTER. Named as Camillo Antonio Polistena's father on his death act. The Polistena quarter had NO documented ancestor above Camillo Antonio at all; this is the first, and his wife Anna Pontillo is the second. DATED AND GIVEN A TRADE: thirty-eight and a MARINARO in December 1836. That sets the Polistena beside the Arena and the Arlotta as another Scilla sailing family, and it is the first fact about him that is not a name on his son's death act. AND A DEATH BOUND AT LAST: «il FU Giuseppe» and «la FU Anna Pontillo» in their son Camillo Antonio's marriage act of 23 JANUARY 1881, each «residente in vita in Scilla». Both were alive at their daughter Fortunata's birth in January 1840 and dead by January 1881. A THIRD AGE, AND IT DOES NOT AGREE: he is FIFTY in September 1844 (Nati 1844 atto 137), against thirty-eight in December 1836 and thirty-four in December 1833. Births of 1794, 1798 and 1799. The two earlier figures agree with each other and this one does not; recorded, not averaged.

name: Giuseppe Ventrice
registerNote: Giovanna's father, and he died TWO DAYS BEFORE HER THIRD BIRTHDAY. Act 12 of Briatico Morti 1831, read in the original: dead at two in the morning on 21 June 1831 in his own house, «di anni TRENTA», declared by Giacomo Comerci, a miller, and Rosario Zungri, a bracciale. THE YEAR CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE: the certified copy in the marriage bundle was read as 1839 and published that way; the original says 1831 and the rest of the 1839 register agrees it cannot be. HIS AGE IS STILL IN DISPUTE — thirty at death (born c. 1801) against the thirty-three he gave for HIMSELF when he registered Giovanna's birth in June 1828 (born c. 1795). The archive carries his own declaration and keeps the other on the record. HE MARRIED AT ZAMBRONE ON 2 MARCH 1824, a contadino of thirty-four born at S. COSTANTINO, and the act calls him «figlio DEL FU DOMENICO e DELLA FU ANNA MAROPOLI» -- so BOTH HIS PARENTS WERE DEAD by then, which dates his mother's death for the first time. On the surname MAROPOLI against this archive's ANNA FAMA, see the corrections page.

name: Gregorio Melluso
registerNote: BURIED AT MAREEBA, in far north Queensland -- Section 4 Catholic, Row I, Plot 10 -- a long way from the Brisbane the rest of this family settled in, and his registration is marked C for a country event. His parents GENNARO MELLUSO and MARIA LIMARDO come from that registration, which this archive has held since before today; what it lacked was the people.

name: Leonardo Russo
registerNote: Concetta Russo's father, living at Scilla in 1885. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Litteria Morabito
registerNote: FILIPPO ARENA'S MOTHER, wife of Orazio Arena (b. c. 1751). Present in person at her son's marriage on 12 November 1815 and giving her consent with her husband. THE NAME IS LITTERIA, AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG FOR AN AFTERNOON: the civil act's hand gives something like «Setteria», but her son's BAPTISM EXTRACT, copied into the marriage bundle in Latin by the parish economo on 26 May 1815, writes «ex Horatio Arena et LITTERIA MORABITO coniugibus». Litteria is a real and common name on this coast -- from the Madonna della Lettera, patroness of Messina, across the strait -- and «Setteria» is not. The clearer document wins. Not in the family tree. SHE OUTLIVED HIM: Orazio died 12 July 1830 and she is named without «fu» in the 1838 marriage Tavola, so she was still alive on 4 September 1838, a widow of eight years.

name: Lorenzo Costa
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 1 June 1915 (Antonio Costa)
registerNote: GENEROSA COSTA'S PATERNAL GRANDFATHER, named on her father's death act. He is a generation above anything this archive held on the Costa side, which until today stopped at Antonio Costa «b. c. 1840».

name: Maria Assunta Melluso
registerNote: THE FIRST PROSTAMO EVER FOUND IN THE QUEENSLAND INDEX, and she was born a MELLUSO. She is buried at Mount Gravatt as MARIA ASSUNTA PROSTAMO in plot 3B-607, immediately beside DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO in 3B-608 -- husband and wife by the adjacent-plot rule. A MELLUSO MARRIED A PROSTAMO A SECOND TIME, two generations after Alfonso Prostamo married Caterina Melluso at Briatico on 21 May 1887; HOW SHE JOINS ALFONSO'S LINE IS UNTESTED and a repeated surname pairing is a hint, not a descent. Trove has her independently, naturalised 4 July 1966 at 3 Frank Street, Graceville. THE TWO DATES RECONCILE: she DIED on 27 October 1991 and was BURIED on the 30th.

name: Maria Catalano
registerSources: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
registerNote: ROSARIO MAZZA'S MOTHER, named in his birth act of 2 June 1845 and nowhere in the family tree. The parish of the CHIESA MAGGIORE returned the baptism notice the same day. She and Mariano were both thirty-six, so both born about 1809 -- which puts their marriage in the window the Piedimonte MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI cover from 1841, a series this archive has never opened. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «e della VIVENTE MARIA CATALANO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi». The same certificate that gives her husband. It is also the first record of her TRADE -- industriosa, the word these registers use for a woman doing piecework at home.

name: Maria Costa
registerSources: Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 89 read in the processetti of 1851
registerNote: Giovanni Arlotta's wife. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. NOTE THE SURNAME: she is the SECOND Costa in this generation -- Filippo Arena's wife is Domenica Costa -- and their great-grandson Rocco married a THIRD, Generosa Costa. A Lorenzo Costa was also lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. CONFIRMED TWICE, by the 1851 marriage act and the 1830 birth act.

name: Maria Currenti
registerSources: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original
registerNote: VENERA CASSANITI'S MOTHER, dead by October 1872 -- «e di FU MARIA CURRENTI». AND SHE CORRECTS A READING OF MY OWN MADE AN HOUR EARLIER: the 1848 annual Tavola band, read at 640 pixels, gave her as «Venuti Maria». The marriage act, read at full width, says CURRENTI. Same class of error as the Bonanno/Bonaccorso confusion in the same sweep, and the same remedy -- a name off a contact sheet is a hypothesis, not a reading.

name: Maria Donato
registerNote: A daughter of MICHELE DONATO and MARIA SOFI, and a sister of Nunziata Donato, dead at two years and four months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her death act gives her father's trade -- PESCATORE -- and the family's address.

name: Maria Limardo
registerNote: GREGORIO MELLUSO'S MOTHER, from the same registration and likewise already recorded, never surfaced. LIMARDO IS A POTENZONI SURNAME -- it appears in the Potenzoni birth index of 1818 -- which places this Melluso household in the Briatico-Potenzoni district rather than among the Agrigento Melluso that fill Geneanet. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria Martello
registerNote: Giuseppe Arena's wife -- Giuseppe being Rocco Arena's brother, born 5 March 1860. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her father PAOLO MARTELLO was already RESIDENT IN AMERICA in 1885.

name: Maria Teresa Polistina
registerNote: GIUSEPPE ARENA'S WIFE, and an ARENA-POLISTINA marriage a century before the two surnames meet again in this family. Both her parents were dead by November 1821. NOTE WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this archive's Polistena line at Scilla is not connected to her, and Polistina is a common name in the town.

name: Maria Vecchio
registerNote: ANGELA CRUPI'S MOTHER, and named in FOUR of her children's Queensland death registrations -- Angela's, Pietro's, Antonino's and Mario's. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria de Amico
registerNote: Nunziata Sofi's mother. Not in the family tree. HER NAME IS CONFIRMED TWICE, by her daughter's birth act of 1818 and by the 1844 Tavola independently, which is why the Tavola's reading of the OTHER mother in the same entry is a question rather than a verdict -- see [[Marta Paladino]]. NOTE A COINCIDENCE, NOT A JOIN: the Michele Donato of act 31 of 1845 married an ANGELA DE AMICO. De Amico is common at Scilla and nothing yet connects the two women.

name: Marianna Musumeci
registerSources: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 (4 April 1890), read in the original
registerNote: GENERATION SEVEN, Rosario Nicotra's mother, named in his death act of 1890 as «fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA» — dead by then. Musumeci is among the commonest surnames in both Giarre and Mascali, so she cannot be traced on the name alone; what she gives is the second half of a couple and a maiden surname to search.

name: Mariano Mazza
registerNote: SALVATORE MAZZA'S ELDER BROTHER, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM. Rosario Mazza's first son is named for ROSARIO'S OWN FATHER -- exactly what the custom predicts -- which is a third independent pointer at Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809) after the 1845 birth act and the «di Mariano» patronymic. Born in CONTRADA SAN BASILIO, the same lane the family is in when Salvatore is born eleven months later. ELEVEN MONTHS IS TIGHT: Salvatore was born 5 January 1873, so either this boy died in infancy or the two births are ten and a half months apart. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought. NOTE THE NAME: there are now THREE Mariano Mazza in this archive -- this baby, his grandfather (b. c. 1809), and the twentieth-century man in the family tree who is a son of the Orazio born 1883. All three are TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE twice over -- this baby of 1872, his grandfather born about 1809, and the tree's twentieth-century namesake -- and they are filed apart on purpose so that no father= in this file can resolve to the wrong one.

name: Mariano Mazza
registerSources: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
registerNote: THE TOP OF THE SICILIAN SPINE, AND HE HAS BEEN FILED ON THE WRONG MAN. His son's birth act names him in his own words; his son is entered as «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO» in the 1873 birth of Salvatore and again in the 1871 marriage. THE NAMESAKE TRAP, AND THIS ARCHIVE WALKED INTO IT: the family tree holds a «Mariano Mazza» who is the son of the ORAZIO MAZZA BORN 1883, himself a son of Rosario -- a twentieth-century man who cannot have fathered a boy in 1845. The 1845 record was attached to that slug and sat on his person page until 20 September. He is filed here as «Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809)» so no parent link can ever resolve to the wrong one. Not in the family tree. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871, AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS SO IN A PRINTED FIELD. The publication certificate for his son Rosario's marriage reads «figlio del VIVENTE MARIANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi» -- not the absence of a «fu» but the positive word, written into a form that has a blank for exactly this. He was about sixty-two, still a bracciante, still living at Piedimonte Etneo. TWENTY-SIX YEARS AFTER his own appearance at the comune house to declare Rosario's birth, and the second document in which he speaks for himself rather than being named by a descendant.

name: Mario Crupi
registerNote: A THIRD BROTHER OF ANGELA CRUPI, same parents again. A «Mariano Crupi» marries on 31 January 1940 -- the two names are interchangeable in this index.

name: Marta Alfonzetti
registerSources: processetti 1815 n. 29, estratti di battesimo e di morte
registerNote: DOMENICA COSTA'S MOTHER, widowed in March 1790 when her husband was about forty, and still alive in November 1815, when she stood beside her daughter and consented to the marriage. She is named three times in one bundle -- in her daughter's 1787 baptism, in her husband's 1790 death, and in the 1815 civil act -- which is as firmly as anyone in this archive is attested. ALFONZETTI is a Scilla name met elsewhere in the same run: an Alfonzetti groom marries in 1817 (atto 19). Not in the family tree.

name: Marta Paladino
registerNote: CANDELORO DONATO'S WIFE. HER GIVEN NAME IS IN DISPUTE AND THE DISPUTE IS WORTH KEEPING. Her son's birth act of 18 December 1816, written while she was in the next room, reads «e da MAR-TA PALADINO, di anni trenta, sua moglie legittima» -- the name broken across a line, and the second line beginning plainly «ta». The 1844 marriage Tavola calls her «Paladino MARIA». The act is contemporaneous and primary and the Tavola is an index made up at the year's end, and THIS VERY INDEX SERIES HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT GIVING A MOTHER THE WRONG NAME -- the 1854 Tavola calls Serafina Arlotta «Rosa», and that error briefly made a brother into a cousin. Against that: the same 1844 Tavola gets the OTHER mother in the same entry exactly right, «de Amico Maria», as her own daughter's birth act confirms. So the index is not uniformly careless. MARTA is published here because the act says it; MARIA is recorded because the index says it. Another child of Candeloro in the Scilla births of 1810-1830 would settle it.

name: Michele Donato
registerNote: DOMENICO DONATO'S ELDER BROTHER, and NOT THE MICHELE DONATO OF THIS ARCHIVE'S SPINE. Two men of the name stand three feet apart in these records: this one, born about 1814 at Messina, and his nephew born at Scilla on 3 October 1855 and named for him. Keep them apart. His act is what dates the grandfather — «FIGLIO DI Candeloro Donato», not «del fu», so CANDELORO WAS STILL ALIVE in August 1845 — and it is his mother's surname, PALADINO, that the 1844 Tavola then matched to make the brothers brothers.

name: Orazio Arena
registerNote: THE TOP OF THE ARENA SPINE UNTIL THIS AFTERNOON, AND NOW NOT. He is a MARINARO in every record that gives him a trade, and the sea runs FIVE generations through him: his father Filippo, himself, his son Filippo, his grandson Francesco Antonio, his great-grandson Rocco. He stood at three of his sons' weddings -- Filippo's in 1815, Giuseppe's in 1821, Antonio's in 1828 -- and died at six in the morning on 12 July 1830, in his own house, with two young kinsmen to declare it. HIS OWN DEATH ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS: «figlio del fu FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO». Not in the family tree. AND THE NAMESAKE IS STILL A TRAP: the tree holds an «Orazio Arena» of generation six, father of Teresa Arena, the man it wrongly hangs Rocco Arena under. TWO DIFFERENT MEN, two generations apart.

name: Paolo Ventrice
registerSources: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
registerNote: The deepest name on the bride's side, reached because his son's death act calls him «il fu Paolo». Husband of ANNA PAPPA.

name: Pasquale Donato
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 20 April 1937
registerNote: THE CHILD THE NAMING CUSTOM PREDICTED, FOUND. Row 4 of the work list reasoned that Domenico Donato and Nunziata Sofi should have a PASQUALE for the maternal grandfather Pasquale Sofi. Here he is, with both parents named on his death act, and a wife: GENEROSA COSTA.

name: Pasquale Sofi
registerNote: NUNZIATA SOFI'S FATHER, and a sailor like the Donato men he married into. Alive in July 1844: his daughter's marriage bundle holds no death certificate for him. Not in the family tree.

name: Pasqualina Idone
registerNote: MARIA COSTA'S MOTHER, alive and present at her daughter's wedding on 30 August 1828, consenting with her husband Rocco Costa. IDONE is a Scilla surname this archive has met once before -- a Giuseppe Idone, sixty-four, witnessed Rocco Arena's birth in 1861, thirty-three years later and four generations down the same street.

name: Pietro Crupi
registerNote: ANGELA CRUPI'S BROTHER, and new to this archive. His Queensland death registration of 1961 names FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO -- the same parents as hers. Angela married Rosario Mazza and lies at Nudgee; her brothers were in Queensland too, and nobody here knew it. HE CAME WITH ANTONINO. Both brothers arrived in Brisbane on the OTRANTO on 19 AUGUST 1930, Pietro entered as born 1898 and Antonino as born 1907. AND HE HAS NO ALIENS CARD FOR A REASON: NAA: BP4/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P records «Alien Registration Certificate NOT ISSUED», the folio noting that he was NATURALISED 23 FEBRUARY 1932. By 1939 he was a British subject and outside the series. The absence is explained, not unexplained.

name: Prospero Arena
registerNote: THE SECOND DECLARANT AT ORAZIO ARENA'S DEATH, also «nipote del defonto» and also a MARINARO. Born about 1805, so too old to be a son of Filippo (m. 1815) or Giuseppe (m. 1821) -- which makes nephew more likely than grandson, and would mean ORAZIO HAD A BROTHER. Recorded as a question, not an answer.

name: Raffaele Polistina
registerNote: «RAFAELE POLISTINA, DEFONTO» at his daughter Maria Teresa's promessa on 7 November 1821, and «fu Raffaele» in the Tavola -- so dead before that date. Nothing else is known of him.

name: Rocco Arlotta
registerNote: THE ARLOTTA IN ROCCO ARENA'S HOUSEHOLD in the Manhattan census of June 1900, now identified: he married ANTONIETTA TAVANI in Manhattan on 4 June that same month. His father was ANTONIO Arlotta -- NOT the Giovanni Arlotta who was Serafina's father -- so he is not her nephew; a cousin is likelier and is untested. He stayed in New York: a Rocco Arlotta baptises children at Our Lady of Loretto, the Arena's own parish, in 1905 and 1908. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Rocco Costa
registerNote: MARIA COSTA'S FATHER, a MARINARO, and he STOOD AT HER WEDDING on 30 August 1828 and gave his «espresso e formale consenso» in person. Not in the family tree. NOTE WHAT HE IS NOT: this archive briefly carried a DOMENICO COSTA, commerciante, as a candidate for Maria's father, on the strength of his standing witness at her daughter's registration in 1830. HER FATHER WAS ROCCO. The candidate is withdrawn by the act, which is what candidates are for.

name: Rocco Polistina
registerSources: Scilla, Nati 1833 atto 174, read in the original
registerNote: A SECOND SIBLING OF CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA, three years older than Annunziata. The index spells the mother PONTILLO here, correctly -- the same index got her wrong three years later, which is a useful reminder that an index can be right and wrong about the same woman in the same series. HIS ACT IS ATTO 174 AND IT HAS BEEN READ. It gives his parents' ages -- Giuseppe thirty-four and a MARINARO, Anna thirty-three -- which cross-check his sister's act of 1836 exactly. AND ITS MARGIN CARRIES HIS MARRIAGE: «L'anno 1869, il giorno 12 Luglio ... ha contratto matrimonio in questo Comune con COLORINA BRI[...]». He lived to thirty-five and married at Scilla on 12 JULY 1869; the bride's name is cut by the binding and is recorded as read, uncertain. Not in the family tree.

name: Rosario Nicotra
registerSources: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 — all read in the original
registerNote: FOUND, 9 October 2026, in Mascali Morti 1890 atto 35. «è morto NICOTRA ROSARIO, di anni NOVANTA CIRCA, CONTADINO, residente in Mascali, NATO IN GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA, MARITO DI MURABITO VENERA», died 4 April 1890 at contrada Montargi. After three documents he has a birthplace, a birth year, a trade, a death, two parents and his wife named beside him. He was BORN AT GIARRE about 1800 — which is very likely why his son Giovanni said «nato a Giarre» — and he had moved to Mascali by 1872. Three independent acts now name him: his son's marriage in 1872, his granddaughter's birth in 1873 where he is «di Rosario» and alive, and his own death.

name: Santa Ungaro
registerNote: ORAZIO ARENA'S MOTHER, and the second person of generation nine on this side. «Della FU Santa Ungaro» in her son's death act of July 1830, so dead before then. UNGARO is a surname new to this archive. Nothing else is known of her and nothing else is likely to be: Scilla's civil registers begin in 1809, fifty-eight years after her son was born.

name: Santo Arena
registerNote: THE FATHER OF TWO ARENA GROOMS AND NOT OURS. His son ROCCO married Domenica Costa on 10 June 1821 and his son FRANCESCO married Concetta Palermo on 13 December 1833; both entries give the mother as VITTORIA FIORENZA, which is what makes them brothers. The 1833 entry writes «fu Santo», so he was dead by then; the 1821 entry's father's name is cut by the page edge and this is what supplies it. NO CONNECTION TO ORAZIO ARENA IS CLAIMED -- Scilla holds at least seven Arena households in this period.

name: Serafina Arena
registerSources: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms, Our Lady of Loretto and Most Precious Blood (Findmypast) — US/NY/CATH/PR/BAP/01054593
registerNote: ROCCO ARENA AND GENEROSA COSTA'S SECOND NEW YORK CHILD, and not in the family tree. Named SERAFINA — which is her paternal grandmother's name, SERAFINA ARLOTTA, exactly as Calabrian custom prescribes for a first daughter born after the family's own Anna. The naming custom followed them across the Atlantic.

name: Serafina Arena
registerNote: A CHILD THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW EXISTED, found while trying to prove something else. Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa had a daughter SERAFINA born at Scilla about May 1912 who lived three months. SHE IS THE SECOND SERAFINA: the first was baptised at Our Lady of Loretto, Manhattan, on 15 August 1898, and the couple gave the name again in Calabria fourteen years later -- the same reading this archive makes of their TWO SONS NAMED ANTONIO. NOTE WHAT SHE PROVES INCIDENTALLY: the household was at Scilla and still having children in 1912, which is the return from America seen from the inside, and GENEROSA COSTA was bearing a child at about forty-four. Her father is «ROCCO, MARINARO» here and «PESCATORE» on his own death act of 1932.

name: Serafina Arlotta
registerNote: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are now confirmed twice over: Giovanni Arlotta, marinaro, and Maria Costa.

records.what: Scilla, Nati 1854, atto 76 — a fourth child, Giovanni, 30 April 1854

corrections: Her father GIOVANNI ARLOTTA came in person to declare this grandson, aged seventy-five, and gave the boy his own name. She is entered as twenty-two; her own birth act of 1830 makes her twenty-three and ten months.

name: Serafina de Luca
registerNote: ANTONIO ARENA'S WIFE, married at Scilla on 10 August 1828. Her father FILIPPO DE LUCA was already dead -- «fu Filippo» -- and her mother ANNA ALFONZETTO was living. NOTE THE SURNAME, AND NOTE THAT NOTHING IS CLAIMED FROM IT: Alfonzetto is the same name as MARTA ALFONZETTI, Domenica Costa's mother, who was alive at Scilla in 1815. Two Alfonzetti women in one family's circle is what a small town looks like, not a connection.

name: Simone Nicotra
registerSources: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35 (4 April 1890), read in the original
registerNote:
GENERATION SEVEN, AND THE OLDEST NICOTRA THIS ARCHIVE HAS REACHED on the line that leads to the children. Named in his son's death act: «NICOTRA ROSARIO ... nato in GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA». Dead by April 1890, and since Rosario was born about 1800 at Giarre, Simone was fathering children there at the turn of the century — before Sicilian civil registration began in 1820, which is why no birth act for Rosario can exist.
A SIMONE NICOTRA IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE. Giarre's very first register year, Nati 1820, holds two untitled Nicotra households and one of them is SIMONE NICOTRA x DADONE. A man fathering a child at Giarre in 1820 and a man fathering Rosario at Giarre about 1800 are entirely consistent, and the forename is uncommon. IT IS NOT JOINED. The 1820 act names a wife this one does not match, and a shared forename in one town is exactly the trap this archive has refused a dozen times. The test is Giarre's pre-1820 parish registers or a Mascali marriage act for Rosario and Venera.

name: Teresa Arena
registerNote: Orazio Arena's earliest known child. Not in the family tree -- which gives Orazio only the two children who turn out to be Francesco Antonio's.

name: Teresa Arena
registerSources: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Teresa Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/08/1943, Padre Giuseppe, Madre Serafina Vita, Coniuge Gaetano Cosentino»
registerNote: GRANDDAUGHTER OF DOMENICO ARENA AND TERESA POLISTINA, and named for her grandmother exactly as the custom predicts. She died at Scilla on 27 August 1943, wife of GAETANO COSENTINO. Her line is a cousin branch of this archive's own: her great-grandfather ORAZIO ARENA is Filippo's father. NOTHING HERE JOINS HER TO THE SPINE beyond that shared great-grandfather, and nothing should.

name: Teresa Polistina
registerNote: DOMENICO ARENA'S WIFE, married 4 September 1838, and the SECOND Polistina daughter of «fu Raffaele e Letteria Morabito» to marry a son of Orazio Arena -- MARIA TERESA POLISTINA married his brother GIUSEPPE in 1821. EITHER TWO SISTERS MARRIED TWO BROTHERS, OR ONE WIDOW MARRIED HER BROTHER-IN-LAW. Nothing read so far settles it; the Scilla death registers of 1821-1838 would. Recorded as two people because the two Tavole give two different given names, and merging them would be a guess.

name: Venera Murabito
registerSources: Mascali, Morti 1890 atto 35, read in the original
registerNote: GIOVANNI NICOTRA'S MOTHER, of MASCALI, named without «fu» and so alive on 7 October 1872. A contadina. The tree's own household holds a daughter VENERA NICOTRA, and a first daughter is named for the paternal grandmother -- though her mother was a Venera too, so the custom points both ways here and is not evidence on its own. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE, like every person above generation four on this side. ALIVE ON 4 APRIL 1890. Her husband's death act calls him «MARITO di Murabito Venera» — marito, not vedovo, and that register writes «vedovo» for a widower on the same pages. So she outlived him, and her death act is the next document to find: it would give her age, her parents, and the Murabito household she came from.

name: Vittoria Mollo
registerNote: CATERINA CICHELLO'S MOTHER, «la fu Vittoria Mollo» in her daughter's marriage act of 1824. Entirely new. NOTE THE SURNAME: a MOLLO appears twice more in the Zambrone marriages of these years -- Pasquale Piatto's mother is an Anna Mollo in 1823 -- so the Mollo were a Zambrone family and she was probably local.

name: Vittoria Morabito
registerNote: MARIA TERESA POLISTINA'S MOTHER, dead before November 1821. AND THE ARCHIVE'S TWO WITNESSES DISAGREE ABOUT HER NAME: the annual Tavola writes «Vittoria Morabito» and the act itself appears to write «Litteria Morabito, defonta» -- which is the name of the GROOM'S living mother. Two women of the name, or a clerk's eye slipping up a line. The Tavola is preferred here only because it does not repeat itself, and the doubt is recorded rather than hidden. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from Litteria Morabito either way: one was alive that day and one was not.
